speaker: Unknown
en: I'm excited to be here.

speaker: Unknown
en: For those that don't know, 60 seconds, what is LangChain and where do you like sit in the stack?
zh: 对于那些不了解的人,用 60 秒介绍一下,LangChain 是什么,你们想处于技术栈的什么位置?

speaker: Unknown
en: We build tools to make it easy to build agents.
zh: 我们构建让构建智能体变得容易的工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we build developer tools primarily.
zh: 所以我们主要构建开发者工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have an open source framework, which basically connects the model to everything else that you need to build a useful agent.
zh: 我们有一个开源框架,它基本上把模型连接到构建一个有用的智能体所需要的其他一切东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So tools, data, computation, things like that.
zh: 比如工具、数据、计算,诸如此类。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we also have LangSmith.
zh: 然后我们还有 LangSmith。

speaker: Unknown
en: LangSmith is observability and evals.
zh: LangSmith 是可观测性和评估。

speaker: Unknown
en: Agents go wrong all the time.
zh: 智能体总是出错。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you know how they go wrong and how do you measure them so that you can increase their performance over time?
zh: 你如何知道它们怎么出错的,你如何衡量它们,以便你能够随时间提升它们的性能?

speaker: Unknown
en: That's what LangSmith does.
zh: 这就是 LangSmith 做的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why is it difficult to build agents?
zh: 为什么构建智能体很困难?

speaker: Unknown
en: The hard part about building agents is they don't behave how you want them to behave.
zh: 构建智能体的难点在于,它们的行为不会按照你想要的方式表现。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the models are these non-deterministic black boxes, right?
zh: 模型是这些非确定性的黑盒,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And they take natural language as input, and then they output natural language.
zh: 它们接受自然语言作为输入,然后输出自然语言。

speaker: Unknown
en: And inside the black box, they're also non-deterministic.
zh: 而且在黑盒内部,它们也是非确定性的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what that means is that the input you get is infinite in dimension.
zh: 所以这意味着,你得到的输入在维度上是无限的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It can be anything.
zh: 它可以是任何东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: You put a chatbot in front of someone, they can type anything that they want, right?
zh: 你把一个聊天机器人放在某人面前,他们可以输入任何他们想输入的东西,对吧?

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that makes it really hard to know what they're going to type.
zh: 所以这让人很难知道他们会输入什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then once it goes into this model... And by the way, agents are not just one model call.
zh: 而且一旦它进入这个模型……顺便说一下,智能体不只是一次模型调用。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're a series of model calls, and they're interacting with other tools.
zh: 它们是一系列模型调用,而且它们在与其他工具交互。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you have these small black boxes that are then put inside this large system, and you get basically these cascading types of errors.
zh: 所以你有这些小黑盒,然后被放进这个大系统里,你基本上会得到这些级联式的错误。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you have this very big kind of input space.
zh: 所以你有这个非常大的输入空间。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have this very big output space because two similar inputs can go in and they can arrive at completely different answers.
zh: 你有这个非常大的输出空间,因为两个相似的输入进去之后,它们可能得出完全不同的答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the thing that's making all this hard is the LLM itself.
zh: 而让这一切变得困难的东西,就是 LLM 本身。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes, they're very, very smart, but you don't know exactly what they're going to do, and they change answers based on small changes to the input.
zh: 是的,它们非常非常聪明,但你不确切知道它们会做什么,而且它们会因为输入的微小变化而改变答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you build this system, but it's really non-robust,
zh: 所以你构建了这个系统,但它真的非常不稳健,

speaker: Unknown
en: And so getting this system to behave reliably, like that is the hardest part.
zh: 而让这个系统可靠地运行,那才是最难的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like when we talk about agents three years ago, four years ago to agents today, they've gotten a lot better.
zh: 比如三年前、四年前我们谈智能体,到今天的智能体,它们已经好了很多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the main thing that's happened is one, the models have gotten better.
zh: 而发生的主要事情是,第一,模型变好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And two, we've figured out how to build systems that basically harness these models better.
zh: 第二,我们弄清楚了如何构建能基本上更好地驾驭这些模型的系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that second part, the harnessing of these models is what we focus on.
zh: 而这第二部分,对这些模型的驾驭,正是我们关注的重点。

speaker: Unknown
en: How does your business change in a way that people don't see as the models get better?
zh: 随着模型变好,你的业务会如何以一种人们看不见的方式发生变化?

speaker: Unknown
en: The main way our business changes as the model gets better is we basically have to erase big parts of our product.
zh: 随着模型变好,我们业务发生变化的主要方式基本上是我们必须抹掉我们产品的很大一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what I mean by that, and Cursor said this really well as well, I think this was one of their actual operating principles as a company is like erase the product or delete the product, I think is what they called it, where basically like these models get better and things that you had to do six months ago you no longer have to do.
zh: 我的意思是,就像 Cursor 也说得非常好,我认为这是他们公司真正的运营原则之一,大致是抹掉产品或者说删除产品,我记得他们是这么说的,基本上就是这些模型变好了,你六个月前必须做的事情,你现在不必再做了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so this is very relevant in our open source.
zh: 所以这在我们的开源中非常相关。

speaker: Unknown
en: So our open source is all about basically the harness and the framework for taking these models and helping them do things.
zh: 我们的开源基本上全是关于这个驾驭层和框架,用来使用这些模型并帮助它们做事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the right way to take these models and help them do things changes every month, three months, six months, choose your time period, but it changes pretty rapidly.
zh: 而使用这些模型并帮助它们做事的正确方式,每个月、每三个月、每六个月都会变化,随你选时间周期,但它变化得相当快。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you build for such an uncertain future?
zh: 你如何为这样一个不确定的未来进行构建?

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you just have to get in bed with the labs to know the roadmap so you don't waste six months building something that then narrates?
zh: 你是不是必须跟实验室们深度绑定才能了解路线图,这样才不会浪费六个月去构建一个最后作废的东西?

speaker: Unknown
en: There's no easy answer.
zh: 没有简单的答案。

speaker: Unknown
en: On one hand, what are you going to do?
zh: 一方面,你能怎么办呢?

speaker: Unknown
en: Not build.
zh: 不去构建。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's what I like to say to founders who ask this.
zh: 这就是我喜欢对问这个问题的创始人说的话。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do I do?
zh: 我该怎么办?

speaker: Unknown
en: Stuff is changing.
zh: 东西在变。

speaker: Unknown
en: The models are changing.
zh: 模型在变。

speaker: Unknown
en: If I build something now, it might not be relevant in six months.
zh: 如果我现在构建某个东西,它可能在六个月内就不再相关了。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's the alternative?
zh: 那替代方案是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: You just don't build anything?
zh: 你就什么都不构建?

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think you have to make educated guesses as to what parts are going to be around and what parts aren't going to be around in the future.
zh: 所以我认为你必须做出有依据的猜测,判断哪些部分未来会存在,哪些部分不会存在。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for example, early on, the way that we would do tool calling in LangChain was by having the model generate JSON, DSL, and then parsing it.
zh: 举个例子,早期,我们在 LangChain 中做工具调用的方式是让模型生成 JSON、DSL,然后去解析它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that was something that I think we all thought or knew was like a little bit of a hack at the time, but we had to do it because that was the only way to get it to actually steer things, because you have to get it to do this type of tool calling.
zh: 当时我想我们都认为或者都知道这有点像是一种权宜之计(hack),但我们不得不这么做,因为那是让它真正引导(steer)事情的唯一方法,因为你必须让它做这种类型的工具调用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then a few months later, OpenAI came out with tool calling, and I think we recognized pretty early, and this is like a more native version of tool calling that's directly in the model and in the APIs.
zh: 然后几个月后,OpenAI 推出了工具调用,我想我们很早就认识到,这是一个更原生的工具调用版本,直接内置在模型和 API 中。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think we recognized pretty early on that that was the future, and so we invested a lot of efforts and just completely switched from JSON parsing to this tool calling.
zh: 我想我们很早就认识到那就是未来,所以我们投入了大量精力,完全从 JSON 解析切换到了这种工具调用。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think you have to basically recognize what things are short-term hacks and what things are long-term kind of like will always be there.
zh: 所以我认为你必须基本上认清哪些东西是短期的权宜之计,哪些东西是长期的、会一直存在的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The models will never know your proprietary data.
zh: 模型永远不会知道你的专有数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: They will never be able to actually get the output of APIs.
zh: 它们永远无法真正拿到 API 的输出。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to take their API call, pass it to the API, get the output, and then continue in the loop.
zh: 你必须拿到它们的 API 调用,传给那个 API,拿到输出,然后继续这个循环。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think the system around the model connecting it to other places will always be there.
zh: 所以我认为模型周围把它连接到其他地方的系统会一直存在。

speaker: Unknown
en: But a lot of the hacks we do around chain of thought or planning or tool calling, things that can just be much more closely integrated into the model or into the model API will go away.
zh: 但我们在思维链、规划或工具调用方面做的很多权宜之计,那些可以更紧密地集成到模型或模型 API 里的东西,将会消失。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think you just have to be quick to recognize that and go on.
zh: 我认为你必须快速认清这一点,然后继续前进。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why do we need neutral harnesses?
zh: 为什么我们需要中立的中枢(harness)?

speaker: Unknown
en: We see bluntly very brilliant agent builders from the models themselves.
zh: 我们看到模型自身非常出色地构建智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why does your layer not just get eaten by them?
zh: 为什么你的这一层不会直接被它们吃掉?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the reason we need neutral harnesses is that there is a lot of state that you build up either before you build the agent or as part of the agent running.
zh: 我认为我们需要中立的中枢的原因是,有很多状态(state)是你在构建智能体之前或作为智能体运行的一部分而积累起来的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the state can include things like memory, whether that's short-term memory or long-term memory.
zh: 而状态可以包括诸如记忆(memory)之类的东西,无论是短期记忆还是长期记忆。

speaker: Unknown
en: Memory also comes in different form factors.
zh: 记忆也有不同的形态。

en: Obviously, OpenRouter, incredible company, incredible usage.
zh: 显然，OpenRouter 是一家了不起的公司，使用量很惊人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Had them on the show.
zh: 我请他们上过节目。

speaker: Unknown
en: Love Alex.
zh: 我很喜欢 Alex。

speaker: Unknown
en: Alex is great.
zh: Alex 很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think a lot of why people use OpenRouter and Vercel and other gateways is largely for the model access.
zh: 我认为人们使用 OpenRouter 和 Vercel 以及其他 gateway 的很大原因主要是为了模型访问。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think there's also a difference between a router and a gateway.
zh: 所以我认为 router 和 gateway 之间也是有区别的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I would probably say most of OpenRouter's usage, and Alex obviously knows the numbers a lot better than I do, but if I had to guess,
zh: 所以我不认为会有一个路由既能用于法律、又能用于金融、又能用于编程，而且全都一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would guess a lot of it just comes from being a gateway, not a router.
zh: 我猜其中很大一部分只是来自它作为 gateway，而不是 router。

speaker: Unknown
en: So people specify the model they want upfront, and OpenRouter just provides a single API with a single API key for accessing that.
zh: 也就是说，人们预先指定他们想要的模型，而 OpenRouter 只提供一个单一 API、单一 API key 来访问它。

speaker: Unknown
en: In terms of smart routing, I think that's actually being done way less than people think.
zh: 至于智能路由，我认为实际被做的程度远比人们以为的要低。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think when it's done, it's built into the harnesses by folks like Factory.
zh: 而且我认为当它被做的时候，是由像 Factory 这样的人内置到 harness 里的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think Factory does a tremendous job about this.
zh: 我认为 Factory 在这方面做得非常出色。

speaker: Unknown
en: They've written a number of technical blogs that are very well done in terms of how they do routing.
zh: 他们写了好几篇技术博客，关于他们如何做路由，写得非常好。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think right now, I pretty strongly believe that routing, you have to be harness aware.
zh: 但我现在非常强烈地认为，路由必须是 harness 感知的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to know what the task is.
zh: 你必须知道任务是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to know what the harness looks like.
zh: 你必须知道 harness 长什么样。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I don't think you'll have routing that works for law and works for finance and works for coding and have it all be the same.
zh: 所以我不认为你会有一套路由能同时适用于法律、金融和编程，并且全都用同一套。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's going to be very domain and very harness specific.
zh: 它会非常垂直于领域、非常垂直于 harness。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm sorry, when I listen to you, it seems so unwaveringly obvious that routing should be at the harness layer, given the context and memory that is stored there.
zh: 抱歉，当我听你说话时，感觉路由应该在 harness 层这件事简直毫无悬念地显而易见，鉴于那里存储的上下文和记忆。

speaker: Unknown
en: When I have such an obvious response, I like to understand why am I stupid?
zh: 我们不追求在法律上做到最优或在金融上做到最优，我们只是要做一个全公司通用的聊天机器人。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is the bull case for it being at the gateway layer?
zh: 把它放在 gateway 层的看多理由是什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think when people talk about it at the gateway layer, I think there's maybe like two things that they're talking about.
zh: 我认为当人们谈论 gateway 层时，他们谈论的可能有两件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: So one, it makes it way easier to port.
zh: 第一，它让移植容易得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you can take Claude Code.
zh: 比如你可以拿 Claude Code。

speaker: Unknown
en: People love Claude Code, right?
zh: 人们爱 Claude Code，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: If you tell people, hey, you can't use Claude Code, you have to use this other harness.
zh: 如果你告诉人们，嘿，你不能用 Claude Code，你必须用这个别的 harness。

speaker: Unknown
en: There are other good harnesses out there, but let's pretend for a second that you love Claude Code, and you want to let them keep on using that, but you want to do some semblance of kind of like routing to maybe like a deep seek or an open source model or something like that, then the only way you can do that is at the gateway layer, because you don't control the harness.
zh: 市面上确实有其他好 harness，但让我们假设一下你爱 Claude Code，而你想让他们继续用它，但你想做某种类似的路由，路由到比如 deep seek 或某个开源模型之类的，那么你唯一能做到这一点的方式就是在 gateway 层，因为你控制不了 harness。

speaker: Unknown
en: Side note, this is another argument for open source harnesses that you can control and modify.
zh: 题外话，这也是支持开源 harness 的又一个论据，因为你可以控制和修改它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the second thing is when people talk about kind of like routing at the gateway layer, I think they're oftentimes implicitly assuming that there's a domain.
zh: 然后第二件事是，当人们谈论 gateway 层的路由时，我认为他们往往隐含地假设存在一个领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's kind of like two general domains that you could maybe argue that you can build general routers for.
zh: 大概有两个通用领域，你或许可以论证可以为它们构建通用 router。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I actually think OpenRouter has done this to some extent.
zh: 而且我实际上认为 OpenRouter 在某种程度上已经这样做了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You could argue coding.
zh: 你可以说编程。

speaker: Unknown
en: Coding is like the most popular domain.
zh: 编程是最热门的领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's where all the usage is going.
zh: 所有的使用量都流向那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's build a router that works really good for coding.
zh: 我们来构建一个对编程非常好用的 router。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe we won't be like,
zh: 也许我们不会——

speaker: Unknown
en: Harness aware, but we'll be use case aware.
zh: 是 harness 感知的，但我们会是用例感知的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we know different models are good for different things in coding, and we can put it at the gateway.
zh: 也就是说我们知道不同的模型在编程中擅长不同的东西，我们可以把它放在 gateway。

speaker: Unknown
en: The other thing you could say is, hey, we've got this general chatbot.
zh: 你还可以说的另一件事是，嘿，我们有这个通用聊天机器人。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're not trying to be best in the class at law or best in the class at finance, but we're just going to be a general chatbot across the company.
zh: 我们不是要成为法律领域最顶尖或金融领域最顶尖的，我们只是要做一个覆盖全公司的通用聊天机器人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we can know well enough that if you say, hi, how are you doing?
zh: 而且我们可以足够清楚地知道，如果你说，嗨，你好吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't need Opus for that.
zh: 你不需要为此用 Opus。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can use a cheap model.
zh: 你可以用一个便宜的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I think when people talk about routing at the gateway level, they're implicitly kind of assuming that you're doing either like general purpose chat or coding, and you're not doing like a domain-specific thing.
zh: 所以我认为当人们谈论 gateway 层的路由时，他们隐含地在假设你做的是通用聊天或编程，而不是某个特定领域的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: As soon as you get into a domain-specific thing, I really think it has to be at the harness layer.
zh: 一旦你进入一个特定领域的事情，我真的认为它必须在 harness 层。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're not going to use an off-the-shelf gateway router for that.
zh: 你不会为此用一个现成的 gateway router。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in two to three years' time, you think the majority is within the harness, given the benefits that come from that context.
zh: 所以在两到三年的时间里，你认为大多数会在 harness 内，鉴于由此带来的上下文优势。

speaker: Unknown
en: But for very horizontal tasks, it will sit in gateway.
zh: 但对于非常水平化的任务，它会放在网关里。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's exactly right.
zh: 我认为这完全正确。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're building a vertical agent, I think routing needs to be in the harness.
zh: 如果你在构建一个垂直智能体，我认为路由需要放在 harness 里。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're thinking about a general purpose, horizontal task, like just general chat or coding, it could maybe be in the gateway.
zh: 如果你考虑的是通用的、水平化的任务，比如一般聊天或编程，它也许可以放在网关里。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it a commodity?
zh: 它是商品吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Does everyone just build it?
zh: 是不是每个人都会自己构建它？

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think routing is a commodity.
zh: 我不认为路由是商品。

speaker: Unknown
en: I do think people will build it, but I think building it is quite hard even today.
zh: 我确实认为人们会去构建它，但我认为即便在今天，构建它也是相当难的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think part of the reason for that is the models just change so rapidly.
zh: 而且我认为其中一部分原因是模型变化得太快了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So like you can argue that certain models are better at different things, but then a new Opus or new OpenAI model comes out and it's just better at everything.
zh: 比如你可以说某些模型在不同方面更擅长，但随后一个新的 Opus 或新的 OpenAI 模型发布出来，它在所有方面都更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so then the value of routing kind of goes down.
zh: 这样一来，路由的价值就有点下降了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you trust evals?
zh: 你信任 evals 吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think evals are useful, but I wouldn't trust them fully.
zh: 我认为 evals 是有用的，但我不会完全信任它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what I mean by that is I think a lot of the academic evals that are out there that are used when a lot of the models come out are not really that useful anymore.
zh: 我这么说的意思是，我认为市面上很多学术性的 evals，也就是很多模型发布时用的那些，现在已经不太有用了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think all the models that come out are kind of benchmark maxed against those evals, and so you don't learn a lot.
zh: 我认为所有发布的模型都是针对那些 evals 做过基准极限优化的，所以你学不到很多东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think internal evals that you have and that you build for your domain absolutely can still be useful.
zh: 我认为你为自己的领域构建的内部 evals 绝对仍然可以是有用的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I would...
zh: 所以我会……

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, this is the main reason that building evals is such an important part of building a vertical-specific agent.
zh: 我的意思是，这就是构建 evals 是构建垂直领域智能体如此重要一部分的主要原因。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you have to have some way of measuring things.
zh: 我认为你必须有某种衡量事物的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think you can generally trust those evals.
zh: 而且我认为你通常可以信任那些 evals。

speaker: Unknown
en: But even then, one of the most important things to do is just look at the data.
zh: 但即便如此，最重要的事情之一就是直接去看数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just look at the data and see what it's doing.
zh: 直接去看数据，看它在做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Don't rely too much on a single number.
zh: 不要太依赖单一数字。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think this is why you want to have traces.
zh: 我认为这就是为什么你会想要有 traces。

speaker: Unknown
en: You want to look at what's going on.
zh: 你想看看正在发生什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe your evals aren't perfect.
zh: 也许你的 evals 并不完美。

speaker: Unknown
en: Evals are really hard.
zh: Evals 真的很难。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can have some sense, but maybe models are doing better, but in just a different way that you didn't know how to capture before.
zh: 你可以有一些感觉，但也许模型确实做得更好了，只是以你以前不知道如何捕捉的不同方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I do think, yes, I think you can trust vertical specific benchmarks, but you have to evolve those as well.
zh: 所以我确实认为，是的，我认为你可以信任垂直领域的 benchmarks，但你也必须不断演进它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's one of the main things that we've seen because these models just get better in different ways.
zh: 而这是我们观察到的主要事情之一，因为这些模型会以不同的方式变得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can I ask you, you mentioned traces there.
zh: 我能问你一下吗，你刚才提到了 traces。

speaker: Unknown
en: If traces are exhaustive agent work, where is the value then?
zh: 如果 traces 是智能体工作的穷尽记录，那价值在哪里呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: Is it the app, the observability layer, the model layer?
zh: 是在应用层、可观测性层，还是模型层？

speaker: Unknown
en: Where is it?
zh: 价值在哪里？

speaker: Unknown
en: If you're building an agent, I think the value is at what makes that agent good at the domain or vertical that you're working in.
zh: 如果你在构建一个智能体，我认为价值在于让那个智能体在你所工作的领域或垂直方向上出色的是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what I mean by that is, again, I think there's different ways to control what an agent does.
zh: 我这么说的意思是，再强调一次，我认为有不同的方式来控制一个智能体做什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's the context, there's the harness, and there's the model.
zh: 有上下文，有 harness，还有模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: Having specific proprietary things for any of those can be an advantage.
zh: 在其中任何一项上拥有特定的专有东西都可以是一种优势。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think controlling the context is the easiest and the most obvious thing to do when starting.
zh: 我认为在起步阶段，控制上下文是最容易、最显而易见的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that would be data.
zh: 那就是数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that would be data, that would be memory, that would be specific APIs, specific tools that you can use.
zh: 那就是数据，就是记忆，就是特定的 API、你可以使用的特定工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: Controlling the harness is a little bit harder, but you can still put a lot of your domain knowledge around what should do, both routing and things in there.
zh: 控制 harness 有一点更难，但你仍然可以把很多你的领域知识放在里面，包括路由和其中的其他东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the model is the hardest control, but potentially the highest ceiling.
zh: 然后模型是最难控制的，但潜在上限最高。

speaker: Unknown
en: The thing that lets you iterate on each of those is evals and traces.
zh: 而让你能在这每一项上迭代的，就是 evals 和 traces。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there is a ton of value in these, but there's only value in that you capture insights that you bring back to the context, or bring back to the harness, or bring back to the model.
zh: 所以这些里面有巨大的价值，但其价值只在于你捕捉到洞见，并把它们带回到上下文，或带回到 harness，或带回到模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that exact process can look different.
zh: 而这个具体的过程可以呈现为不同的样子。

speaker: Unknown
en: So post-training, great for bringing these insights from traces back to the model.
zh: 比如后训练，非常适合把这些来自 traces 的洞见带回到模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: For bringing things back to the context or memory, you're probably going to want to run another agent over those traces and then have that agent output learnings from memory.
zh: 要把这些东西带回到上下文或记忆，你可能会想要在那些 traces 上运行另一个智能体，然后让那个智能体输出从记忆中得到的经验教训。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then for bringing these learnings in the traces back to the harness, you're probably going to want to run an agent over those traces and update the code of the harness itself.
zh: 然后要把 traces 中的这些经验教训带回到 harness，你可能会想要在那些 traces 上运行一个智能体，并更新 harness 本身的代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we actually have something that does this for people.
zh: 而且我们实际上有一个产品可以帮人们做到这件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's called Engine.
zh: 它叫 Engine。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's an agent in LangSmith that runs over traces and tries to update code.
zh: 它是 LangSmith 里的一个智能体,会在 trace 上运行并尝试更新代码。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then when you update these things, you're going to need to know that it's actually better.
zh: 然后当你更新这些东西之后,你需要知道它是否真的变好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is where evals come in handy.
zh: 而这正是 evals 派上用场的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can I ask, how does continual learning change agents and how they work?
zh: 我能问一下吗,持续学习会如何改变智能体以及它们的运作方式?

speaker: Unknown
en: Continual learning, I don't think so much changes how agents work, but I think it changes the systems that you want to have running around the agent.
zh: 持续学习,我不认为它那么大程度上改变了智能体的运作方式,但我认为它改变了你想在智能体周围运行的系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what I mean by that is I think the core loop for a continual learning agent, the core inner loop maybe to say, will still largely be the same.
zh: 我的意思是,我认为持续学习智能体的核心循环,或者说是核心内循环,基本上仍将保持不变。

speaker: Unknown
en: It will be an LLM running a loop, calling tools, interacting with the model in an environment.
zh: 它将是一个运行循环的 LLM,调用工具,在环境中与模型交互。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think what continual learning adds is an outer loop, an outer loop that looks at the exhaust of agents and then does things with it.
zh: 我认为持续学习增加的是一个外循环,一个观察智能体"废气排放"并对其进行处理的外循环。

speaker: Unknown
en: And again, what it does could be different depending on what continual learning means for you.
zh: 再说一次,它具体做什么取决于持续学习对你来说意味着什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think continual learning is also one of those words that doesn't have a super precise definition.
zh: 所以我认为持续学习也是那些没有特别精确定义的词之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: How would you define it?
zh: 你会怎么定义它?

speaker: Unknown
en: I would define it as a system that gets better over time as it runs.
zh: 我会把它定义为一个在运行过程中随着时间推移而变得更好的系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: And again, there's different ways it could get better over time.
zh: 再说一次,它随时间变好有多种方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: It could update the context, it could update the code of the harness, or it could update the weights of the model.
zh: 它可以更新上下文,可以更新 harness 的代码,或者可以更新模型的权重。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the outer loop will look roughly the same for all of those.
zh: 而外循环对这几种情况来说大致是一样的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It will look like take traces, get learnings, fix something, measure it to make sure it improved, and then repeat.
zh: 它会是:获取 trace,提炼经验,修复某个东西,测量以确保它改进了,然后重复。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that exact changing, again, updating weights of model, very different from updating a text file that is like a memory file.
zh: 但具体改动什么,再次强调,更新模型的权重,与更新一个类似记忆文件的文本文件是非常不同的。

speaker: Unknown
en: If we look at the context layer, we mentioned data being a part of that.
zh: 如果我们看上下文层,我们提到过数据是其中的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're seeing data companies scale to hundreds of millions of revenue in the fastest time ever.
zh: 我们看到数据公司以前所未有的最快速度扩展到数亿美元的收入。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, ever, ever, ever.
zh: 我是说,前所未有、前所未有、前所未有。

speaker: Unknown
en: And everyone is selling data.
zh: 而且每个人都在卖数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you expect this market to play out, given your neutrality on not being involved in it, but being adjacent to it?
zh: 鉴于你持中立立场、不参与这个市场但与之相邻,你预期这个市场会如何发展?

speaker: Unknown
en: Will this be a market of consolidation in years to come?
zh: 未来几年这会是一个整合的市场吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you see it play out?
zh: 你怎么看它的发展?

speaker: Unknown
en: I actually think the data market is still pretty early in the grand scheme of things in so much as we're talking about a context layer for agents.
zh: 我实际上认为,从大局来看,数据市场仍处于相当早期的阶段,因为我们说的是智能体的上下文层。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what I mean by that is there are a bunch of databases that are... ClickHouse is maybe a really good example of one that's doing incredibly well recently.
zh: 我的意思是,现在有一大堆数据库……ClickHouse 可能是最近表现极其出色的一个好例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think they're still largely focused on their database, their good old-fashioned database.
zh: 我认为它们在很大程度上仍然专注于它们的数据库,它们那个老派的数据库。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're good at storing data and querying data, but it's still in pretty traditional ways.
zh: 它们擅长存储数据和查询数据,但方式仍然相当传统。

speaker: Unknown
en: ClickHouse existed pre-AI.
zh: ClickHouse 在 AI 之前就存在了。

speaker: Unknown
en: When we talk about a context layer for agents, and again, there will be a bunch of data produced from software systems and great.
zh: 当我们谈论智能体的上下文层时,再说一次,软件系统会产生大量数据,这很好。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think existing databases, ClickHouse, Mongo, Elastic, whatever, are great for that.
zh: 我认为现有的数据库,ClickHouse、Mongo、Elastic 之类,对此都很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: When we talk about a context layer for agents, I think a key part of what exists there is yes, there's a database.

en: I think Benchmark, when Miles and really the whole Benchmark partnership invested in us, it was me and Ankush.
zh: 我觉得当 Miles 以及整个 Benchmark 合伙团队投资我们的时候,当时只有我和 Ankush。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were two people.
zh: 我们当时只有两个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: We really thought of them as kind of like a third co-founder.
zh: 我们真的把他们当作第三位联合创始人。

speaker: Unknown
en: When I think about company building from two people to where we are now today, which is like 400 people,
zh: 当我回想从两个人把公司做到我们今天这样——大约 400 人——

speaker: Unknown
en: They've been kind of like our most consistent kind of like partner in that journey for sure.
zh: 他们确实一直是我们在这段旅程中最稳定的伙伴。

speaker: Unknown
en: I am not a VC.
zh: 我不是风险投资人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've never done VC.
zh: 我从没做过 VC。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's probably also other market dynamics where great benchmarks involved and that signals thing.
zh: 可能还有其他市场动态,比如 Benchmark 参与其中本身就是一个信号。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're very lucky to have Sequoia join us after like two months, three months after the benchmark round.
zh: 而且我们非常幸运,在 Benchmark 那轮之后大约两三个月,红杉加入了我们。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they've been a tremendous partner as well.
zh: 他们也是一位非常出色的伙伴。

speaker: Unknown
en: Who was it from Sequoia?
zh: 红杉那边是谁?

speaker: Unknown
en: Sonya from Sequoia, who is one of the most plugged in people in the spaces.
zh: 红杉的 Sonya,她是这个圈子里消息最灵通的人之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do their styles differ?
zh: 他们的风格有什么不同?

speaker: Unknown
en: Benchmark is maybe a little bit more what's the core nucleus of the company and we're going to be a sounding board for that and we're going to kind of help with that.
zh: Benchmark 可能更偏向于——公司的核心是什么,我们会为此充当顾问板,我们会在这方面提供帮助。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what I mean by that is I feel like a lot of the company building things, positioning things, I would go to them for and they would spend time there.
zh: 我这么说的意思是,很多公司建设的事情、定位的事情,我都会去找他们,而他们会在这上面花时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: Sequoia's style, I think, is they help with everything.
zh: Sequoia 的风格,我觉得是他们什么都帮。

speaker: Unknown
en: They are just a machine.
zh: 他们就是一台机器。

speaker: Unknown
en: So they help with recruiting of ICs, of executives.
zh: 所以他们帮着招 IC、招高管。

speaker: Unknown
en: They help with marketing and launches.
zh: 他们帮着做营销和发布。

speaker: Unknown
en: Does it really work?
zh: 真的有用吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think so, yeah.
zh: 我觉得有,是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I mean, we've gotten a lot of our candidates from Sequoia references.
zh: 我是说,我们的很多候选人来自 Sequoia 的推荐。

speaker: Unknown
en: Really?
zh: 真的吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 我是第一次创业的创始人,我基本上把所有时间都花在产品上。

speaker: Unknown
en: They have a talent network and we've gotten a bunch of really, really strong candidates from there.
zh: 他们有一个人才网络,我们从那里拿到了很多很多非常强的候选人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Would you say to founders it's worth taking a discount for Sequoia?
zh: 你会对创始人们说,为 Sequoia 打折是值得的吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think absolutely it's worth taking a discount for Sequoia and Benchmark and probably other of these top one or tier one VC firms, but those are the ones that we work with.
zh: 我觉得为 Sequoia 打折绝对值得,Benchmark 也是,可能还有其他这些头部的或一级的 VC 公司也值得,但我们合作的就是这几家。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you know now about fundraising that you wish you could tell yourself when it was just the two of you?
zh: 关于融资,你现在知道了什么,是你希望在当时只有你们两个人的时候就能告诉自己知道的?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there is like this game to fundraising almost.
zh: 我觉得融资几乎有点像一场游戏。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I definitely didn't know that going in.
zh: 我在进入之前肯定不知道这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm a first time founder, like where I spend all my time is on product basically.
zh: 我是第一次创业的创始人，我基本上把所有时间都花在产品上。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I'm very focused on that.
zh: 所以我非常专注于那个。

speaker: Unknown
en: I do think there is this game to fundraising where you want to fundraise without fundraising.
zh: 我确实觉得融资有这个游戏的成分,就是你想在「不融资」的状态下融资。

speaker: Unknown
en: You want to like, once you get one term, you want to get one term sheet and then, you know, tell others you have a term sheet and post a revenue graph on Twitter and then it leads to
zh: 你想要的是,一旦你拿到一个 term,你想拿到一份 term sheet,然后,你知道,告诉别人你有一份 term sheet,在 Twitter 上发一张营收曲线图,然后就会带来

speaker: Unknown
en: All these inbound.
zh: 所有这些主动上门的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you fucking like this?
zh: 你他妈喜欢这个吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: I fucking hate it.
zh: 我他妈讨厌死了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe I'm too old for this game now.
zh: 也许我现在对这场游戏来说太老了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just posturing.
zh: 这就是摆姿态。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like, Harrison, do you really like me and want to build a business with me?
zh: 就像,Harrison,你真的喜欢我、想和我一起做生意吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll give you the same price and the same money than whatever.
zh: 我会给你同样的价格和同样的钱,不管别的什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's just do this.
zh: 我们就这么干吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: Stop fucking posturing.
zh: 别他妈摆姿态了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't like fundraising at all.
zh: 我一点都不喜欢融资。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think, kind of what you were saying, I want to build something great with people I enjoy working with.
zh: 我觉得,有点像你刚才说的,我想和我喜欢共事的人一起做出伟大的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think, yeah, especially for the scale of ambitions that we have, we need to fundraise to get that done.
zh: 我觉得,是的,尤其是以我们野心所在的规模,我们需要融资来实现它。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that was the approach that Benchmark kind of took when we were fundraising from them as well.
zh: 我觉得这也是 Benchmark 在我们向他们融资时所采取的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, hey, let's figure out if we like each other and want to work together.
zh: 就是,嘿,我们先搞清楚我们是否喜欢彼此、是否想一起共事。

speaker: Unknown
en: By the way, that was very good negotiating by them, and so I think they're very good negotiators as well.
zh: 顺便说一句,那是他们非常出色的谈判,所以我觉得他们也是非常好的谈判者。

speaker: Unknown
en: But when I look at our most recent rounds that we've done, we raised from Tom at IVP, our Series B. I had been chatting with Tom from I think right around the Sequoia round for over two and a half years.
zh: 但当我看我们最近完成的几轮时,我们从 IVP 的 Tom 那里融了 B 轮。我从大约 Sequoia 那一轮前后开始就和 Tom 聊了两年半多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so that was a relationship that we just built up over time.
zh: 所以那是一段我们随时间慢慢建立起来的关系。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I got to know him and he got to know me.
zh: 我逐渐了解了他,他也逐渐了解了我。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so when it came time to fundraising, I feel like there was less games involved there.
zh: 所以到了融资的时候,我感觉那里的博弈成分就少了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I really appreciated that.
zh: 我真的很感激这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would love to do a quick fire round.
zh: 我想来一个快问快答环节。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I say a short statement and you give me your immediate thoughts.
zh: 我说一个简短的陈述,你给我你的即时反应。

speaker: Unknown
en: Does that sound okay?
zh: 听起来可以吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's do it.
zh: 来吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: What was your single favorite VC meeting?
zh: 你最喜欢的一次 VC 会面是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: First pitch with Benchmark.
zh: 和 Benchmark 的第一次 pitch。

speaker: Unknown
en: So many legends in the room.
zh: 房间里有那么多传奇人物。

speaker: Unknown
en: Who was the coolest to hang with?
zh: 和谁相处最酷?

speaker: Unknown
en: Bill Gurley.
zh: Bill Gurley。

speaker: Unknown
en: Were you intimidated?
zh: 你当时感到胆怯了吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think I was too naive to be intimidated.
zh: 我觉得我当时太天真了,都不知道胆怯。

speaker: Unknown
en: He's also just like a big man.
zh: 他也是个高大的男人。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's an intimidating figure looming over you.
zh: 是个让你感到压迫的威严身影。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is the single most important thing you believe about agents that most of the ecosystem would disagree with?
zh: 你所相信的关于智能体的最重要的一件事是什么,而生态系统中的大多数人会不同意?

speaker: Unknown
en: It's still really hard to build them, like really, really hard.
zh: 构建它们仍然非常难,真的、真的非常难。

speaker: Unknown
en: Maybe people would agree with that, but I think it's just underrated how hard it is.
zh: 也许人们会同意这一点,但我认为它的难度被低估了。

speaker: Unknown
en: What have you changed your mind on most in the last 12 months?
zh: 在过去 12 个月里,你改变想法最多的是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: MARKET FOR INFERENCE IS MASSIVE.
zh: 推理市场是巨大的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I REMEMBER TALKING WITH THE BOARD ABOUT WHETHER WE SHOULD DO A GATEWAY A YEAR AND A HALF AGO AND WE DIDN'T SEE WHAT VALUE WE COULD ADD OVER SOMETHING LIKE OPEN ROUTER AND I THINK THAT WAS 100% THE WRONG DECISION.
zh: ——(此条无译文)

speaker: Unknown
en: WHAT'S BEEN THE HARDEST TECHNICAL THING FOR YOU AND THE TEAM TO BUILD?
zh: 对你和团队来说,构建起来最困难的技术东西是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: We built our own database for storing agent traces, SmithDB.
zh: 我们为自己的智能体轨迹存储构建了自己的数据库,SmithDB。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you think about competing with ClickHouse and being a customer?
zh: 你如何看待与 ClickHouse 竞争,同时又做它的客户?

speaker: Unknown
en: Kind of weird or normal?
zh: 是有点奇怪还是很正常?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there are 500 different companies that we are frenemies with, and so I think I've personally gotten very used to it.
zh: 我认为有 500 家不同的公司和我们既是朋友又是对手,所以我觉得我个人已经非常习惯了。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can invest in one IPO, OpenAI at $1.5 trillion or Anthropik at $2 trillion?
zh: 如果你可以投资一个 IPO,是 1.5 万亿美元的 OpenAI,还是 2 万亿美元的 Anthropik?

speaker: Unknown
en: OpenAI.
zh: OpenAI。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think they have more diverse, different paths to really tremendous exits valuations.
zh: 我认为他们拥有更加多元化、不同的路径,通向真正惊人的退出估值。

speaker: Unknown
en: Totally get that.
zh: 完全理解。

speaker: Unknown
en: What do you know now that you wish you'd known when you started in 2022?
zh: 你现在知道的、但你希望在 2022 年开始时就已知道的事情是什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: I wish I knew what harnesses today looked like so we could have built them earlier.
zh: 我希望我当时知道今天的 harness 是什么样子,这样我们就能更早地构建它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: Final one for you.
zh: 最后一个问你。

speaker: Unknown
en: What are you most excited for when you look forward five years?
zh: 展望未来五年,你最期待什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm really excited for what creative things we can do with AI.
zh: 我非常期待我们能用 AI 做出的创造性事物。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think a lot of what we work on is helping enterprises be more efficient and delivering outcomes.
zh: 我认为我们做的很多工作是帮助企业变得更高效并交付成果。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think creative things like Suno are tremendously interesting, and I wish we'd see more of those.
zh: 我认为像 Suno 这样的创造性事物非常有趣,我希望我们看到更多这样的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Totally agree.
zh: 完全同意。

speaker: Unknown
en: I remember having Mikey on the show.
zh: 我记得请 Mikey 上过节目。

speaker: Unknown
en: That was a fun one, actually.
zh: 那期其实很有趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: This has been so much fun to do, Harrison.
zh: Harrison,做这期节目非常开心。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you so much for putting up with my waywardness and divergent schedules, but you've been an amazing guest.
zh: 非常感谢你忍受我的任性和反复变化的日程安排,但你是一位非常棒的嘉宾。

speaker: Unknown
en: No, thank you so much for having me.
zh: 不,非常感谢你们邀请我。

speaker: Unknown
en: But before we leave you today, what do Uber, Cursor, and Harvey have in common?
zh: 但在今天和你道别之前,Uber、Cursor 和 Harvey 有什么共同点?

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, they made the really wise decision to build on Fireworks.
zh: 嗯,它们都做出了在 Fireworks 上构建这个非常明智的决定。

speaker: Unknown
en: Fireworks is the specialized intelligence platform behind many of the world's leading AI products.
zh: Fireworks 是许多世界领先的 AI 产品背后的专业智能平台。

speaker: Unknown
en: Companies use Fireworks to deploy the latest open models, specialize them with their own data, and run them in production with the speed and reliability modern AI applications demand.
zh: 各公司使用 Fireworks 部署最新的开源模型,用它们自己的数据进行专业化,并以现代 AI 应用所要求的速度和可靠性在生产环境中运行。

speaker: Unknown
en: But getting models into production is only the beginning.
zh: 但把模型投入生产只是开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: As AI usage scales, the best model for one request isn't always the best model for the next.
zh: 随着 AI 使用规模的扩大,对某个请求最好的模型并不总是对下一个请求最好的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, that's where Fireworks Nexus comes in.
zh: 这就是 Fireworks Nexus 的用武之地。

speaker: Unknown
en: Nexus connects to the AI coding tools and harnesses your engineers already use and intelligently routes each request to the best model for the job, helping you optimize for quality, latency, and cost without changing how your engineers work.
zh: Nexus 连接到你的工程师已经在使用的 AI 编程工具和 harness,并将每个请求智能路由到最适合该任务的模型,帮助你优化质量、延迟和成本,而无需改变工程师的工作方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: To see intelligent model routing and practice, visit fireworks.ai forward slash 20VC to create a free account and use the promo code 20VC50 to claim $50 in credits for 20VC50.
zh: 要在实践中查看智能模型路由,请访问 fireworks.ai 斜杠 20VC 创建免费账户,并使用促销码 20VC50 领取 50 美元的额度,兑换码为 20VC50。

speaker: Unknown
en: While fireworks powers AI, LARADIN helps you measure its impact.
zh: Fireworks 为 AI 提供动力,而 LARADIN 帮助你衡量其影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every company now runs two workforces, humans and AI agents.
zh: 现在每家公司都运营着两支劳动力队伍:人类和 AI 智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: Laredin is the first unified dashboard across both workforces that measures their work and optimizes their impact.
zh: Laredin 是首个覆盖两支劳动力队伍的统一仪表盘,衡量它们的工作并优化其影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: Laredin answers four questions.
zh: Laredin 回答四个问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: Who's using AI?
zh: 谁在使用 AI?

speaker: Unknown
en: Which tools?
zh: 哪些工具?

speaker: Unknown
en: What is it costing?
zh: 成本是多少?

speaker: Unknown
en: And what's it actually being produced for every team across every vendor?
zh: 而对于每个团队、每个供应商,它实际产出了什么?

speaker: Unknown
en: AI ROI stops being a guess and becomes a number that you can consistently and confidently measure.
zh: AI 的投资回报率不再是一个猜测,而是变成一个你可以持续且自信地衡量的数字。

speaker: Unknown
en: Gainsight, Vertiv, SurveyMonkey, and many other enterprise organizations run their AI programs on Laredin.
zh: Gainsight、Vertiv、SurveyMonkey 以及许多其他企业组织都在 Laredin 上运行他们的 AI 项目。

speaker: Unknown
en: Thousands of AI tools and millions of dollars of AI spend are measured.
zh: 数千个 AI 工具和数百万美元的 AI 支出正在被衡量。

speaker: Unknown
en: You bet on AI, Laredin proves that it's working.
zh: 你押注了 AI,Laredin 证明它是有效的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Visit Laredin.com to learn more.
zh: 访问 Laredin.com 了解更多。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's L-A-R-R-I-D-I-N.com.
zh: 那是 L-A-R-R-I-D-I-N.com。

speaker: Unknown
en: While Laredin tracks AI impact, Superhuman helps you move faster.
zh: Laredin 追踪 AI 的影响力,Superhuman 帮你更快行动。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can I be honest with you for a second?
zh: 我能跟你说句实话吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: Here's what my week actually looks like.
zh: 我这一周实际上是这样的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Back-to-back meetings all day and the real pressure builds up in the gaps between them.
zh: 一整天连轴转的会议,真正的压力在会议之间的间隙里积累。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll come out of six founder meetings with a whole stack of follow-ups waiting.
zh: 我参加完六个创始人会议,出来时堆积了一整套待跟进事项。

speaker: Unknown
en: And my inbox, it's hundreds of messages.
zh: 还有我的收件箱,里面有几百条消息。

speaker: Unknown
en: And somewhere in there is the one thing that really matters, which I always tell my mother is her.
zh: 而其中某个地方有那件真正重要的事——我一直告诉我妈妈,那就是她。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've tried AI tools for this, but they always lived in another tab.
zh: 我为此试过 AI 工具,但它们总是存在于另一个标签页里。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'd have to stop, go find it, paste in the context, write the perfect prompt.
zh: 我得停下来,去找它,粘贴上下文,写出完美的 prompt。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was just enough friction that it never really stuck.
zh: 摩擦刚好大到让它从来没能真正坚持用下去。

speaker: Unknown
en: Superhuman Go from the makers of Grammarly is totally different.
zh: 来自 Grammarly 制作方的 Superhuman Go 完全不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's right there where you need it, when you need it, in the doc, when I'm reading, the email I'm writing, when a thread gets dense, I highlight it and ask Go to pull out what matters without losing my place.
zh: 它就在你需要它的地方、在你需要它的时候——在文档里,在我阅读时,在我正在写的邮件里,当一个线程变得密集时,我高亮它并让 Go 提取出重要的内容,而不会丢失我的位置。

speaker: Unknown
en: And after a run of back to backs,
zh: 而在一连串连轴转的会议之后,

speaker: Unknown
en: I ask what was actually decided, and Go turns it into clear action items or drafts, the reply I need to send.
zh: 我会问实际上决定了什么,Go 会把它变成清晰的行动项或草稿,即我需要发送的回复。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's already up to speed, and I'm always the one in control.
zh: 它已经掌握了最新情况,而始终是我这个人在掌控。

speaker: Unknown
en: Try Superhuman Go from the makers of Grammarly, and find out more at superhuman.com.
zh: 试试来自 Grammarly 制作方的 Superhuman Go,在 superhuman.com 了解更多。
